title: Perf canary baseline store + versioning (per model/version/SKU) and update policy
creator: Nadia Rahman
description: Implement baseline storage strategy for perf-canary regressions. Baselines must be stable and queryable per model + model version + runtime version + hardware SKU (and optionally region/tier), with an explicit update/promotion policy to avoid drift-induced alert storms. Includes decisions on where baselines live (object storage vs config service), versioning scheme, retention, and how to handle seasonality/slow fleet changes.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline artifacts can be fetched by perf-canary given a stable lookup key (model + model_version + runtime_build + kernel_tag + hardware_sku + workload_profile + region(optional)).
Baselines are immutable once written; new baselines are created as new versions and promoted explicitly.
Promotion flow is auditable (who/when/why) and supports rollback to a prior baseline.
Policy defined for when to create vs reuse baselines across runtime releases, kernel changes, and fleet/driver changes.
Noise controls: minimum sample sizes and smoothing assumptions documented; baseline drift/seasonality risks explicitly addressed.
Operational runbook notes added for baseline refresh/backfill and emergency freeze.
content:
Context
- perf-canary will continuously issue synthetic requests against a curated model set to detect regressions in p95 latency and tokens/sec. This ticket covers baseline persistence + versioning so that:
  (1) comparisons are apples-to-apples (same model/version/workload/hardware)
  (2) we can evolve baselines safely without baseline drift creating false positives
  (3) SRE/runtime can quickly attribute changes to runtime builds/kernels/fleet

Problem statement
- We need to compare observed canary metrics against a "known-good" baseline distribution per model. If baselines update implicitly (rolling), slow infra changes (driver, GPU mix, noisy neighbors) can shift baseline and either mask real regressions or generate alert storms.
- Baseline cardinality can blow up if we key on too many labels (region x tier x sku x runtime x model x prompt bucket). We need a principled key and promotion policy.

Decision summary (aligned w/ ADR: perf-canary baseline + thresholds)
1) Baseline artifacts are stored in object storage (baseline-bucket) as immutable, versioned JSON artifacts.
   - Rationale: cheap, immutable, supports large payloads (histograms/quantiles), can be produced by benchmark-lab job and consumed by perf-canary.
2) Control plane stores only a pointer (baseline_ref) per canary target with an explicit "promoted" baseline version.
   - Rationale: control plane config is the audited source of truth for what baseline is currently used for alerts/gates, without stuffing large artifacts into config.
3) Baselines are versioned and promoted explicitly (no automatic rolling baseline in MVP).
   - We may add a "rolling candidate" baseline later for visualization only, but alerts/gates use the promoted baseline.
4) Key dimensions for baseline lookup:
   Required:
   - model_id (canonical registry name)
   - model_version (registry version / digest)
   - runtime_build_id (or runtime_semver + build hash)
   - hardware_sku (e.g., a100-80gb, h100-sxm)
   - workload_profile_id (synthetic prompt distribution version, e.g., canary-v0)
   Optional (configurable):
   - region (enabled only where we have known region-level perf deltas; default off)
   - capacity_tier (hosted|dedicated) (default off for MVP; use separate workload profiles if needed)
   - kernel_tag (stored in artifact metadata; NOT part of primary key in MVP to avoid explosion)

Baseline artifact schema (stored in object storage)
- filename convention:
  baselines/{model_id}/{model_version}/{hardware_sku}/{workload_profile_id}/{runtime_build_id}/baseline-{created_at}-{baseline_version}.json
- top-level fields (informational; exact structure in artifact):
  - baseline_version: monotonically increasing integer per key
  - created_at
  - created_by (service or human promotion)
  - source_run_id (benchmark-lab job id) + links
  - window: sample count, duration, environment notes
  - telemetry_schema_version
  - metrics:
    - e2e_latency_ms: p50/p95/p99 + histogram buckets
    - runtime_latency_ms (if available)
    - queue_time_ms
    - prefill_ms / decode_ms
    - tokens_per_sec: mean + p50/p95 + distribution summary
    - batch_size distribution
    - kv_cache_hit_rate (optional; recorded when emitted)
  - tags: runtime_build_id, kernel_selection_id (if present), driver version (if available), fleet annotation

Promotion policy
- Two-step process:
  A) Create baseline artifact from controlled load (benchmark-lab) or approved canary capture window.
  B) Promote baseline by updating control-plane canary config (baseline_ref -> new baseline_version).
- Promotion requirements:
  - Minimum N samples per prompt bucket and aggregate (exact N in ADR; enforced by baseline generator).
  - Must run on the target hardware SKU with the target runtime build.
  - Must pass sanity checks: p95 within expected bounds vs prior baseline (guardrail, not strict).
- Rollback:
  - Control-plane config keeps last 3 promoted versions; rollback is a config change to previous baseline_ref.

Handling drift and seasonality
- The canary uses synthetic prompts and fixed QPS caps. This intentionally reduces seasonality vs customer traffic.
- Known drift vectors we must account for:
  1) Fleet composition changes (mixed GPU stepping, BIOS/driver updates)
  2) Runtime scheduling heuristic updates affecting batch size distribution
  3) Kernel selection auto-changes
- MVP approach:
  - Do NOT update baseline automatically; baseline changes only when we deliberately promote.
  - Add annotation fields in the artifact to capture driver/fleet context when available; use them in triage.
  - Optional region-specific baselines remain off by default; enable only for regions with consistent deltas and enough sampling.
- Follow-up (ENG-4882):
  - Consider "dual baseline" (promoted baseline for paging + rolling candidate for dashboards) to detect slow drift without breaking alert stability.
  - Explore SKU-aware thresholds rather than region-aware baselines where possible.

Integration points
- perf-canary baseline fetch + evaluator: perf-canary PR-19218 will read baseline_ref from config and fetch artifact from baseline-bucket.
- baseline generation job: benchmark-lab PR-18990 outputs artifacts in the expected path and writes a manifest for promotion.
- telemetry schema: relies on runtime build tags + kernel identifiers (redwood PR-19193) and model version tags (model-registry PR-18577).

Operational notes
- Access control: perf-canary service account has read-only access to baselines bucket path(s) for its region + environment; baseline generator has write access.
- Retention: keep all baseline artifacts for 180 days (or longer for top models); promoted baselines pinned (never GC’ed) while referenced by config.
- Emergency freeze: if alert storm suspected due to a bad baseline promotion, revert baseline_ref and disable new promotions until incident is resolved.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we need to include kernel_tag in the primary key once kernel auto-selection becomes more dynamic? (Current stance: no; store as metadata + rely on canary attribution metrics.)
- Should dedicated capacity pools have their own baselines even on same SKU? (Likely yes via workload_profile_id/tier split, but defer until phase-2 coverage.)

Links
- Confluence ADR (baselines/thresholds): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-perf-canary-baseline-and-thresholds.json
- Kickoff notes: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/perf-canary-kickoff-notes.json
- Cardinality audit: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/perf-canary-metrics-cardinality-audit.json

comments: 2026-01-08 (Nadia Rahman): Created. Baseline storage is the critical dependency for canary evaluator. Proposal: immutable artifacts in object storage + promoted pointer in control plane config. Avoid rolling baseline initially to prevent drift masking regressions.

2026-01-10 (Logan Wright): +1 to object storage for artifacts; please keep config payload small. Also: ensure we don't key on region by default—too much cardinality and different retention costs per region.

2026-01-12 (Noah Patel): Added proposed key dimensions. Pushing back on kernel_tag in key for MVP; we'll rely on kernel_selection_id as attribution metric + metadata. If we key on kernel_tag we’ll explode baselines during auto-selection experiments.

2026-01-15 (Sofia Ivanova): From scheduler side: baselines should include batch size distribution and queue_time_ms; otherwise we can't tell scheduler regressions vs GPU execution regressions. Please ensure these are in artifact schema even if not all models emit KV cache signals.

2026-01-18 (Hiro Tanaka): Agree with keeping kernel_tag out of key. But baseline artifact must store kernel_selection_id (or equivalent) so when we see a regression we can correlate quickly to kernel rollouts. Otherwise triage will be slow.

2026-01-22 (Allison Grant): Alert hygiene: explicit promotion + rollback is mandatory. Please also document that promoted baselines should not be overwritten (immutability) and that baseline promotions are change-managed like any other prod config.

2026-01-27 (Nadia Rahman): Implemented artifact path convention and manifest format in benchmark-lab job. Added sanity checks: min sample size, stable p95 within guardrail vs previous baseline (non-blocking warning).

2026-01-31 (Noah Patel): Wired perf-canary baseline fetch to baseline_ref pointer in control plane (pending PR-19218). Added caching of baseline artifacts in-memory with TTL to avoid hammering bucket.
2026-02-03 (Sean Gallagher): Concern: region deltas are real for some fleets. OK to keep region out of key, but please make it config-toggleable for phase-2 so we can opt-in where needed.

2026-02-07 (Noah Patel): Marking as ready. Baseline artifacts immutable + promoted pointer path done. Added runbook note: rollback baseline_ref first if alert storm starts immediately after promotion.
2026-02-14 (Nadia Rahman): Closed as Done after us-east phase-1. Follow-up ENG-4882 filed for drift detection (rolling candidate baseline) and region-specific thresholds vs baseline explosion.
